evidence: ch16 panel 20: "Wrapping (chapter 8): a new receipt that says where, with parseLine's receipt inside." go/ch8.html line 457: "Later (chapter 19) you'll meet %w, which also lets a program look inside a receipt"; line 913 also says "(chapter 19)". grep finds no "wrap" anywhere in go/ch8.html.

what: The parsons exercise accepts only one order, but moving `totals := tally(hauls)` above the error check also compiles and prints exactly the goal output, so a correct solution is marked wrong.
evidence: Scratch run of loot/main.go with body order hauls,err / totals := tally(hauls) / if err != nil {...} / fmt.Print(report(totals)) on Go 1.27.3: prints the same 5-line table for haul.txt (exit 0), and for bad.txt it prints the same `loot: line 2: ...` error with exit 1. The prompt only says "the error message must be printed before the program exits, and nothing can use hauls before it exists", and both alternatives meet that.
fix: Add to the prompt: "Check the receipt straight after reading, before using hauls at all." (or pin line 14).

what: The boss parsons accepts only the source order, but two other orders of main's six lines give identical output and get marked wrong.
evidence: Scratch runs of boss_parsons.go with Go 1.27.3: order 17,18,21,19,20,22 (move l.Room = "attic" before Toggle) and order 17,18,19,21,20,22 (move it before the second print) both print "hall false / true / attic true", the same as the key.
fix: Make line 20 `fmt.Println(l.Room, l.On)`. Then each alternative prints `attic true` on line 2 instead of `hall true`, so only one order matches. Recapture and update the explain text.

what: The page says every Go binary is statically linked by default. That's only true for pure-Go programs: with cgo on (the Linux default when a C compiler is installed), programs that import net or os/user link libc dynamically.
evidence: "A Go binary is statically linked by default: the runtime, the garbage collector and every package you imported are inside the one file"
fix: "A pure-Go program like loot is statically linked: ..." and optionally add "(programs that use cgo, for example through net on Linux, may depend on the system C library)".

what: The test terminals show `go test -v | sed ...` with go test's exit code 1, but a reader running that pipeline gets sed's exit code 0. The hidden `; exit ${PIPESTATUS[0]}` that keeps the 1 is disclosed only in the footer.
evidence: board_s1.cmd real step: "cd loot_s1 && go test -v | sed -E 's/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+s/…s/'; exit ${PIPESTATUS[0]}". Panel 30 uses data-exit, so it shows exit 1 under the shown pipeline. The footer says "a small shell wrapper, exit ${PIPESTATUS[0]}, not shown".
fix: Add one clause to panel 30's caption: "the exit code shown is go test's own; in your shell, `echo $?` after a pipe reports sed's 0 unless you `set -o pipefail`".

what: The alias card says an alias "Has exactly the original's methods, and you can't add more." That's false when the alias names a type from your own package: methods can be declared through it.
evidence: Scratch run on Go 1.27.3: `type Celsius float64; type Reading = Celsius; func (r Reading) Twice() Reading { return r * 2 }` compiles and prints 42 for Celsius(21).Twice(). Panel 21 correctly limits the rule to non-local types such as float64.
fix: "Has exactly the original's methods; you can't add methods to float64 through it (panel 21)."

evidence: Panel 32: "Called with nothing: nums is an empty slice of type []int". Notebook: "with no arguments at all, nums is also nil (length 0 either way)". The Go spec: "the value passed to p is nil".
